title: NOW and TODAY mark the formula syntactically volatile with PtgAttrSemi even inside untaken branches
statement: In Excel 16.0.20527, NOW() and TODAY() take zero arguments, refuse any argument or call postfix at formula entry, and set the formula's syntactic volatility token (PtgAttrSemi) regardless of whether the call sits in an executed branch (so IF(C1=2,TODAY(),0)*0 with a false condition still recalculates on Calculate). When evaluated against the workbook clock in the 1900 date system, NOW()*0 and TODAY()*0 evaluate to 0.
basis: Measured across Excel 16.0.20527.20088 in prefix_metadata (rows 303 and 330), excel-entry.tsv (4 NOW and 3 TODAY entry rows), and volatility probes p1a/p1b/p2 in VOLATILITY.md.
